concepts.title: Health and Disease
concepts.definition: Health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease, while a disease is any disturbance in the normal functioning of the body that impairs health.
concepts.key_idea: Health is a positive state of well-being; disease is a negative deviation from the normal healthy state.
question_patterns: what is meant by health
define the term disease
difference between health and disease
why is health called the ultimate treasure
what do you understand by health and disease

solution_steps.explain: Health covers physical, mental and social wellness, not just absence of illness.
A disease is any change from the normal state that causes discomfort or malfunction of the body.
Disease is the negation of health; maintaining health through good habits prevents disease.

worked_examples.question: Is a person who has no visible disease always healthy? Explain.
worked_examples.solution: No. Health includes physical, mental and social well-being. A person with no obvious disease may still be unhealthy if they are mentally stressed or socially isolated.
worked_examples.answer: Not necessarily; health is a complete state of well-being, not merely absence of disease.

worked_examples.question: Why is health considered the ultimate treasure?
worked_examples.solution: Without health a person cannot work, learn or enjoy life. All achievements depend on a healthy body and mind, so health is valued above wealth.
worked_examples.answer: Because every other achievement depends on good health.

concepts.title: Types of Diseases: Infectious and Non-infectious
concepts.definition: Infectious diseases spread from one person to another through agents like air, water or vectors, while non-infectious diseases do not spread and are caused by internal factors such as deficiency, genetic defects or lifestyle.
concepts.key_idea: Infectious diseases are communicable; non-infectious diseases are non-communicable.
question_patterns: what are infectious diseases
what are non-infectious diseases
difference between infectious and non-infectious diseases
give examples of communicable diseases
classify a disease as infectious or non-infectious

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether the disease is caused by an external agent like a pathogen or an internal factor.
Find out whether the disease can pass from an infected person to a healthy person.
If it spreads, it is infectious; if it does not spread, it is non-infectious.

worked_examples.question: Classify cold and diabetes as infectious or non-infectious.
worked_examples.solution: Cold is caused by a virus and spreads through air droplets, so it is infectious. Diabetes is caused by the body's inability to regulate sugar and does not spread, so it is non-infectious.
worked_examples.answer: Cold is infectious; diabetes is non-infectious.

worked_examples.question: Is cancer an infectious disease? Give reason.
worked_examples.solution: Cancer results from uncontrolled cell division within the body and is not caused by a pathogen that can spread to others, so it is non-infectious.
worked_examples.answer: No, cancer is non-infectious because it does not spread from person to person.

exercises.question: List three infectious diseases and three non-infectious diseases.

concepts.title: Causes of Diseases: Pathogens, Deficiency and Genetic
concepts.definition: Diseases are caused by pathogens such as bacteria, viruses, fungi and protozoa, by deficiency of nutrients such as vitamins and minerals, or by genetic defects inherited from parents.
concepts.key_idea: Different diseases have different causal agents: living pathogens, lack of nutrients, or faulty genes.
question_patterns: what are the main causes of diseases
name the types of pathogens that cause disease
how does nutrient deficiency cause disease
what is a genetic disease
give one example each of a pathogenic, deficiency and genetic disease

solution_steps.explain: Check whether the disease is due to a pathogen, a nutrient deficiency or an inherited gene.
Pathogens cause infectious diseases, deficiencies cause deficiency diseases and faulty genes cause genetic diseases.
For example, malaria is caused by a protozoan, scurvy by vitamin C deficiency and haemophilia by a genetic defect.

worked_examples.question: Identify the cause of scurvy and the cause of malaria.
worked_examples.solution: Scurvy is caused by a deficiency of vitamin C in the diet. Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium spread by the female Anopheles mosquito.
worked_examples.answer: Scurvy: vitamin C deficiency; malaria: protozoan pathogen.

worked_examples.question: Why is haemophilia called a genetic disease?
worked_examples.solution: Haemophilia is caused by a defective gene inherited from the parents, so it is passed through generations and not acquired from the environment.
worked_examples.answer: Because it is caused by an inherited defective gene.

exercises.question: Name four types of pathogens with one disease each.
Explain how a deficiency disease differs from an infectious disease.
Give one example of a genetic disease.

concepts.title: Transmission of Diseases
concepts.definition: Infectious diseases spread from an infected person to a healthy person through air, water, food, physical contact, sexual contact or vectors such as mosquitoes and flies.
concepts.key_idea: Pathogens reach a new host through specific routes called modes of transmission.
question_patterns: how do diseases spread from one person to another
what are the modes of disease transmission
how does malaria spread
name the vector that spreads dengue
explain direct and indirect transmission of diseases

solution_steps.action: identify the pathogen and its source
solution_steps.explain: Find the microorganism and the infected person or animal that carries it.
Determine whether the pathogen travels through air, water, food, contact or a vector.

solution_steps.action: trace the path to the new host
solution_steps.explain: Show how the pathogen enters a healthy person and causes the disease.

worked_examples.question: How does the common cold spread from one person to another?
worked_examples.solution: When an infected person sneezes or coughs, tiny droplets carrying the cold virus are released into the air. A healthy person nearby inhales these droplets and gets infected.
worked_examples.answer: Through air droplets released during coughing or sneezing.

worked_examples.question: Explain how cholera is transmitted through water.
worked_examples.solution: The cholera bacterium present in the faeces of an infected person can contaminate drinking water. A healthy person who drinks this contaminated water develops cholera.

concepts.title: Prevention of Diseases: Vaccination and Hygiene
concepts.definition: Diseases can be prevented by vaccination, which builds immunity, and by maintaining personal and public hygiene such as clean water, clean food and sanitation.
concepts.key_idea: Prevention is better than cure; vaccination and hygiene are the two main preventive measures.
question_patterns: how can diseases be prevented
what is vaccination
why is hygiene important to prevent disease
name some common vaccines given to children
explain how vaccination prevents disease

solution_steps.explain: Vaccines introduce weakened or dead pathogens so the body makes antibodies and memory cells.
Washing hands, bathing and keeping the surroundings clean block the routes of transmission.
Safe drinking water, proper sanitation and clean food prevent the spread of pathogens in the community.

worked_examples.question: How does the polio vaccine protect a child from polio?
worked_examples.solution: The polio vaccine contains weakened polio virus. When given, the child's immune system produces antibodies and memory cells. If the real virus enters later, the body quickly destroys it.
worked_examples.answer: The vaccine trains the immune system to fight the polio virus.

worked_examples.question: Give two hygiene practices that prevent diarrhoeal diseases.
worked_examples.solution: Washing hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet, and drinking boiled or filtered water, prevent the entry of disease-causing germs.
worked_examples.answer: Hand washing and using safe drinking water.

concepts.title: Immune System and Immunity
concepts.definition: The immune system is the body's defence mechanism made of cells, tissues and organs that recognises and destroys pathogens, and immunity is the ability of the body to resist a particular disease.
concepts.key_idea: Immunity may be innate (present from birth) or acquired (developed after exposure or vaccination).
question_patterns: what is the immune system
define immunity
difference between innate and acquired immunity
how do antibodies protect the body
what role do white blood cells play in immunity

solution_steps.explain: The immune system includes white blood cells, antibodies and lymphoid organs.
Innate immunity is present from birth; acquired immunity develops after infection or vaccination.
Antibodies recognise and neutralise specific pathogens so the body resists the disease.

worked_examples.question: Why does a person who has recovered from chickenpox usually not get it again?
worked_examples.solution: During the first infection the immune system makes memory cells. On a second encounter these cells quickly produce antibodies and destroy the virus before it causes disease.
worked_examples.answer: Because memory cells give long-lasting acquired immunity.

worked_examples.question: Distinguish between innate and acquired immunity with one example each.
worked_examples.solution: Innate immunity is present from birth, such as the skin acting as a barrier. Acquired immunity develops after exposure, such as immunity against measles after vaccination.
worked_examples.answer: Innate: skin barrier; acquired: measles immunity after vaccine.

exercises.question: Name the main cells of the immune system.

concepts.title: First Aid
concepts.definition: First aid is the immediate, basic medical help given to an injured or suddenly ill person before professional medical treatment arrives.
concepts.key_idea: Prompt and correct first aid prevents the condition from worsening and can save a life.
question_patterns: what is first aid
what first aid should be given for a minor burn
how to give first aid for bleeding
what to do if a person faints
explain the importance of first aid

solution_steps.explain: Check the person's condition and the cause of injury without endangering oneself.
Apply the correct first aid measure such as washing a burn with cool water or pressing a clean cloth on a bleeding wound.
Call for a doctor or ambulance and keep the person comfortable until help arrives.

worked_examples.question: What first aid should be given for a minor burn on the hand?
worked_examples.solution: Hold the burnt area under cool running water for about 10 minutes to reduce heat and pain, then cover it loosely with a clean cloth. Do not apply ice or any ointment without medical advice.
worked_examples.answer: Cool the burn with running water and cover it loosely.

worked_examples.question: How would you give first aid to a person with a bleeding wound?
worked_examples.solution: Press a clean cloth firmly on the wound to stop the bleeding, raise the injured part if possible, and take the person to a doctor.
worked_examples.answer: Apply pressure with a clean cloth and seek medical help.

exercises.question: Define first aid.
List three items found in a basic first aid kit.

concepts.title: Health and Nutrition
concepts.definition: A balanced diet providing carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins and minerals in correct proportions is essential for maintaining health, and body mass index (BMI) is used to assess whether a person's weight is healthy for their height.
concepts.key_idea: BMI compares weight with height to classify a person as underweight, normal, overweight or obese.
question_patterns: what is a balanced diet
how is BMI calculated
calculate the BMI for a given weight and height
what does a BMI value indicate about health
why is nutrition important for health

solution_steps.explain: Note the body weight in kilograms and the height in metres.
Note the body weight in kilograms and the height in metres.
Divide the weight in kg by the square of the height in metres.
BMI below 18.5 is underweight, 18.5 to 24.9 is normal, 25 to 29.9 is overweight and 30 or above is obese.

worked_examples.question: Calculate the BMI of a person whose weight is 54 kg and height is 1.5 m.
worked_examples.solution: BMI = weight / height^2 = 54 / (1.5 x 1.5) = 54 / 2.25 = 24. Since 24 lies between 18.5 and 24.9, the person has a normal weight.
worked_examples.answer: BMI = 24, which falls in the normal range.

worked_examples.question: A student weighs 72 kg and is 1.6 m tall. Find the BMI and classify the student.
worked_examples.solution: BMI = 72 / (1.6 x 1.6) = 72 / 2.56 = 28.125. Since 28.125 lies between 25 and 29.9, the student is overweight.
